A plan for physical tests

Two explanations may agree on one reading and disagree on another. A timing reference, a reversed path or a different waiting time can help reveal the difference.

Choose a check at the bench. These are proposed ways to test ideas, not measurements being collected here. Better tools can be useful even when the result agrees with existing physics.

Choose a comparison to see which difference it could reveal.

Words used here
control
A comparison designed to test whether an apparent effect could have another explanation.
phase
Where a repeating signal is in its cycle: for example, whether it is rising or falling at a given moment.
Read the fuller explanation

The finesse pathway proposes controlled carriers, coherent transformations, independent references, multichannel records and adversarial inference. Its practical value is not conditional on discovering an anomaly. Better sensing and clearer mechanism identification can remain useful conventional results.

Choose a bench question. A reversible path, an added phase reference or a changed waiting time can expose different collisions between explanations. The proposed controls do not all answer the same question, and none is a substitute for a calibrated apparatus.

This is a design encounter. No acquisition runs behind the glass. The next evidence would include the physical carrier, nuisance envelope, raw records and a decision rule fixed before opening the result.
